expectations.text: At least one documentation file contains BOTH a '## Before You Begin' section (with a prerequisite list or checklist) AND a '## What You Will Learn' section (with bulleted learning outcomes). Both sections must appear in the same file. A file with only one of the two does NOT satisfy this — both are required for a Tutorial per the skill's Phase 3 specification.

The executor produced: README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, DATABASE.md, OPERATIONS.md, RUNBOOK.md, KNOWN_ISSUES.md, ONBOARDING.md — none contain either section. No tutorial-style documentation was generated.

expectations.text: A documentation plan, handoff plan, or index file contains explicit P0/P1/P2 priority markers — the literal strings 'P0', 'P1', or 'P2' must appear as priority labels in a table or section heading. Timing-based language like 'Read First: Yes' or 'Week 1' does NOT satisfy this — the P0/P1/P2 scheme is required.
expectations.evidence: The only P1/P2 occurrences found are in OPERATIONS.md lines 168-172 inside a PagerDuty alert-severity table (e.g., '| Error rate | >1% over 5 min | P2 |', '| Pod crash looping | Any pod restarting >3× in 10 min | P1 |'). These are monitoring alert severity levels, not documentation priority labels for a plan/index file. No P0 appears anywhere. No documentation plan or handoff index with P0/P1/P2 priority labeling was produced.

suggestions.reason: The three assertions all test documentation-generator skill-specific output patterns (Tutorial doc-type, P0/P1/P2 priority scheme, Before You Begin sections). These are strong discriminating assertions that correctly fail for a without_skill run — the without run produced competent general documentation but none of the skill-specific structural conventions. This is exactly the right design.

suggestions.assertion: A documentation plan, handoff plan, or index file contains explicit P0/P1/P2 priority markers
suggestions.reason: Consider also asserting that the P0/P1/P2 labels appear in a document that is explicitly a plan or index file (e.g., README.md reading-order table, a DOC_PLAN.md), not just any file. The current assertion already excludes alert-severity P1/P2 via the 'priority labels in a table or section heading' language, but the file-type qualifier ('documentation plan, handoff plan, or index file') adds meaningful precision worth keeping.

eval_feedback.overall: Evals are well-designed for this without_skill condition — all three test skill-specific conventions that a capable but unaided model will not spontaneously adopt. The 0/3 pass rate is the expected correct result.
